subject: Re: Prompt collection & model-fit follow-up - ACME discovery
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Prompt collection & next steps - ACME discovery

John - thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and asks from our side: 

- Goal: validate model fit for ACME's internal Q&A and summarization flows, with strict PII redaction requirements.
- Next steps we discussed: you to share representative prompt examples + a small set of edge-case inputs (5-10), and we will run an initial eval and share model recommendations + benchmark links.

To help the eval, could you: 
1) Paste 8-12 representative prompts/responses (de-identified if needed) or attach a CSV with one prompt per line.
2) Mark any prompts that absolutely cannot contain customer PII (we'll apply redaction rules).
3) Flag any edge cases (examples that are long, code-like, or include tables).

Attached is a redaction checklist template (redaction_guidance_template.docx) that many customers find helpful for marking PII fields. We'll also produce an anonymized prompt set when we run the eval so you can review outputs without exposing sensitive data.

Rishi and Neha will take it from there once we have the prompt samples. Proposed cadence: you send the prompts by Monday 3/30 EOD, we return a quick model-fit summary and benchmark links by Thursday 4/2.

Thanks -
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0198

Attachments: redaction_guidance_template.docx

From: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Mar 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prompt collection & next steps - ACME discovery

Marissa - appreciate the recap. I attached a small CSV (acme_prompt_samples.csv) with 10 prompts. A couple quick notes inline below and pasted one edge case at the end.

Questions / constraints: 
- Our legal team is strict about customer identifiers (emails, account numbers). We prefer sending de-identified prompts but want guidance on whether the redaction template is sufficient.
- We have a few prompts that include merchant transaction descriptions (sensitive financial context). Those should be treated as high-sensitivity.

Attached: acme_prompt_samples.csv (10 rows). Example edge case pasted here:

---
Prompt: "Summarize the following multi-party support thread between customer A (acct: 12345) and merchant B about chargebacks, include timeline and suggested next steps."
---

Let us know if you'd prefer us to pre-redact the CSV or if Redwood should handle redaction during ingestion.

Thanks,
John
John Doe
Head of Product Data Ops, ACME Corp
john.doe@acme.com

On Sun, Mar 29, 2026 at 09:15 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> (sending initial request)

Attachments: acme_prompt_samples.csv

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Prompt collection & next steps - ACME discovery

John / team - thanks for the sample CSV. Quick read and recommendations before we run the eval: 

1) Redaction: the template Marissa shared covers common PII classes (emails, account IDs, full names). For transaction descriptions and merchant-specific identifiers we recommend either: 
   - Option A: you pre-redact sensitive fields (replace with tokens like [REDACTED_MERCHANT], [REDACTED_TXN_ID]) - fastest and preferred for legal comfort.
   - Option B: we perform redaction in ingestion using your rules - requires a short config and adds an extra review cycle.

2) Model recommendations (initial): 
   - For highest quality on multi-turn summarization and nuanced instruction-following: open-llm-xxl-super (quantized) and redwood-qa-pro-v2 (if you need lower-latency w/ similar quality).
   - For cost-sensitive batch summarization workloads: open-llm-xl-qa (8-bit) with caching.

3) Benchmarks & quality/regression concerns: 
   - We will run the 10 prompts + 20 synthetic edge cases through the models above and produce token-cost, latency P95, and rouge/qa-accuracy metrics.
   - If you have existing ground-truth summaries or an eval rubric, please share - it accelerates regression analysis.

4) Deliverables and timeline: 
   - We will validate redaction approach and run the initial eval. Expect a one-pager with recommended model(s), benchmark links, and a prompt-level failure review.

Links (preliminary):
- Benchmark dashboard (internal): https://drive.redwood.com/teams/acme/benchmarks/llm-fit-2026-03
- Redwood eval docs: https://docs.redwood.com/benchmarks/README.md
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2026-01

Note on quality regression: for production rollouts we recommend maintaining a small daily prompt set (50-100) from production traffic for continuous alerting. We'll help set that up in the Console once you pick a model.

I'll attach a quick eval plan and a redaction checklist after we finalize the ingestion approach.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Attachments: (will include eval_plan_acme_v1.pdf after ingestion is agreed)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prompt collection & model-fit follow-up - ACME discovery

John - perfect, this is exactly what we need. Quick decisions and next steps: 

- Please go with Option A (pre-redact) for the initial eval - saves time and keeps legal happy. Use tokens as Rishi suggested.
- Upload the redacted CSV to the shared Drive folder (link below) and drop a note in this thread when done. We'll pick it up and run the eval.
- Rishi: when you attach the eval plan, include the specific synthetic edge-case generator settings (length distribution, table-like inputs, and code blocks).

Shared drive (drop location): https://drive.redwood.com/teams/acme/benchmarks/llm-fit-2026-03
HubSpot reminder: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2026-01 (set task for evaluation deliverable on 4/2)

Thanks everyone - looking forward to the results.

Marissa
